title: Game Creator Lab
headline: Your kid makes their own 3D video game. For real.
intro: Six weeks, live online, for kids 11 to 15. They design a world, a hero and a story, build the characters in Blender, and make it all playable in Unity, with AI as a helper, not a shortcut. They learn what makes a game good, and they finish one.
price_note: for all 12 live sessions. Can be paid in two parts.
ages_note: A keen 10 year old is welcome with a parent beside them.

cohort.label: Winter cohort
cohort.when: Tuesdays and Thursdays, 4:30 to 6:00 pm Central

apply_note: Applying is free. I reply within a day, check the computer can run Unity, and then send the payment link.
gift: Giving a seat as a holiday present? Say so in the form and I will send a printable gift card.

makes.title: A finished 3D game
makes.text: Playable on Mac or Windows, with a title screen, a level, a goal and a win. Theirs to share.

makes.title: Their own Game Bible
makes.text: The design book real studios keep: pitch, world, characters, story, mechanics, levels, playtests, credits.

makes.title: Their own 3D models
makes.text: Their hero and props from their world, built from scratch in Blender.

makes.title: How to think like a designer
makes.text: Core loops, feedback, level design, difficulty, playtesting. Words and ideas they keep forever.

makes.title: AI used well
makes.text: How to ask AI for ideas and code help, how to check what it says, and why their own ideas come first.

weeks.title: What makes a game fun
weeks.text: Invent a paper game, change one rule, feel the difference. Then the world: its place, its magic rule, its history, and a map.

weeks.title: Characters and first 3D
weeks.text: A hero with a want, a fear and an ability. Then sculpt that hero in Blender from simple shapes.

weeks.title: The world, into Unity
weeks.text: Props that tell a story without words. Then the moment: walking their own hero around their own world.

weeks.title: Mechanics and levels
weeks.text: Collecting, scoring and feedback, a first look at real code, and a level that guides the player without arrows.

weeks.title: Challenge, story and feel
weeks.text: Hazards, checkpoints, winning and losing fairly, a title screen, their own recorded sounds, music and effects.

weeks.title: Playtest and launch
weeks.text: Real players, a fix list, a finished build, and the Family Arcade, where every kid plays their game for the families.

depth: Most kids' coding classes teach a tool. This one teaches game design, and the tools serve it.
Every session starts from a question real designers ask: what is fun, what does the player want, why does this level feel unfair. Every session ends with a page of their Game Bible.
The tools are the real ones. Unity, the engine behind a huge share of the games on phones and consoles, and Blender, the free 3D software film and game studios use. Both free, forever.

ai_rule.title: AI is a helper, not the artist
points: Kids design first, on paper and in their own words. Then we ask AI for twists, code help and error fixes.
In class, AI runs on my screen. Kids ask through the chat, and we read and check every answer together. No child needs an AI account.
Kids never put their name, school, face or any personal detail into an AI tool.
Anything AI helped with goes in the game's credits. Honesty about tools is part of being a creator.

teacher.name: Jordan Larsen
teacher.text: I build games and teach people to build with AI. ROOTSIGNAL is my own 3D game in Unity. Civil X is a game with AR and VR I designed with a team, and The Stellar Alchemist is my comic series turned animated show. I also make music and run Greenfire, a creative technology and land project. I would love to help your kid make the game they keep describing at dinner.
teacher.caption: ROOTSIGNAL, Jordan's game in Unity

computer.title: Check the computer first
points: A Mac (macOS 12 or newer) or a Windows 10 or 11 computer, with 8 GB of memory or more (16 GB is better).
A mouse with a scroll wheel. Blender is very hard with a trackpad alone.
Not a Chromebook, iPad or phone. Unity cannot run on them.
computer.note: Not sure? Tell me the make and model in the form and I will check for you.

safety.title: Safe, small and private
points: Eight kids, one teacher, and parents are welcome to sit in on any session.
First names only in class. Cameras are optional.
I never message a kid privately. Everything goes to the parent's email.
Sessions are not recorded unless every family agrees, and no kid's work, face or name is ever posted without the parent's written yes.
We collect your details, not your kid's: only their age, never their name, school or email.

faq.q: Does my kid need to know how to code?
faq.a: No. We read and change real code together a little at a time, and the starter project does the hard parts. Kids who already code will find stretch goals every week.

faq.q: What does it cost beyond the $500?
faq.a: Nothing. Unity Personal, Blender and the course assets are free. You will need a Mac or Windows computer and a mouse.
Optional side quests of 20 to 40 minutes a week: drawing, building one more thing, or watching a family member play their game.

faq.q: What if my kid misses a session?
faq.a: Every week has a catch up version of the project, so they load it and keep going with their own models and ideas.

faq.q: What kind of game will they make?
faq.a: A 3D adventure: their hero explores their world, collects things, avoids dangers and reaches a goal. It holds every big idea in game design and it is finishable in six weeks. The world, the hero, the story and the twist are all theirs.
A full refund up to 7 days before the first session. After that, a seat in the next cohort. If a class is cancelled, a full refund.

bible.title: Free: print the Game Bible
bible.text: The kids' design workbook from the course: pitch, world map, hero, level design, playtest log and credits. Free to print tonight, whether or not they join.

proof.title: I really make this stuff
proof.intro: Kids can tell when a teacher has never shipped anything. Here is some of what I have built: games, worlds, characters and stories.

items.title: Civil X

items.title: The Stellar Alchemist

items.title: From a drawing to a game
items.text: A young maker painted her own characters on paper, and we turned them into a game she could play. That moment is what this course is for.
